```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(fpp3)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4
)
source("lab_submission.R")

lab_meta <- list(id = "lab07", title = "Midterm prep")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "A large negative ACF spike at lag 1 after an extra difference usually means:",
  q2 = "Across ETS vs ARIMA, the course rule is:",
  q3 = "Over-differencing is something you should:",
  q4 = "Name one midterm trap you will watch for, and how you will avoid it."
)
```

## What you will do

Short exam-style checks. No new models.

Open this file and click **Run Document**. Packages: `fpp3`, `learnr`.
Exercise chunks run when you click Run Code. They are not knitted in one pass.

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("Over-differencing", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Need d=2"),
  answer("Perfect white noise"),
  answer("Seasonal AR of order 12"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("Use hold-out accuracy and residuals, not raw AICc", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Always pick the lower AICc"),
  answer("Always pick ARIMA"),
  answer("Ignore residuals if the point forecast looks smooth"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("Avoid once plots and the ACF already look stationary", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Always do, to be safe"),
  answer("Apply only to white noise"),
  answer("Use instead of a log transform"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q4}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "e.g. accuracy left on the log scale.",
  trim = TRUE
)
```

## Submit

Answer the questions above first, type your name, download the `.txt`, and upload it.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
  }
)
```
